 Thai Nguyen: Livestreaming agricultural product sales opens up livelihood opportunities and reduces poverty in rural areas.
 TPO - Using products from her hometown, Ms. Bui Thi Hai Yen, Director of Ban Viet Production and Trade Service Cooperative, has brought local agricultural products to e-commerce platforms. In addition, the young female director connects and supports the consumption of products for local households, creating more opportunities for employment, increasing income, and developing the rural economy.
 Báo Tiền Phong • 16/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 From local agricultural products to digital brands. 
 Recently, the live stream sales of agricultural products organized by Bui Thi Hai Yen, taking place right in the countryside of Phu Binh ( Thai Nguyen province), have opened up a new way for producers to access the market. Local agricultural products are being introduced directly to consumers through social media platforms. 
 Ms. Bui Thi Hai Yen (born in 1992, from Bac Kan province, Thai Nguyen province) graduated with a degree in Business Administration from Hanoi University of Industry. She has a strong foundation in management, production organization, and business. 
 However, her concerns about local agricultural products were the driving force behind her entrepreneurial journey. She realized that many local products were of good quality but lacked adequate investment in branding, packaging, marketing, and distribution systems. Producers created the products but lacked the resources to access the market, understand customer needs, or build their own brands. 
 Live stream selling agricultural products hosted by Bui Thi Hai Yen 
 In 2023, the Ban Viet Production and Trade Service Cooperative was officially established (in Bao Ly commune, formerly Phu Binh district) with 7 members. The cooperative chose to develop processed products from rice and local agricultural products, with crispy rice being identified as its main product. 
 Using glutinous rice from Thau Dau, a local specialty, Ms. Hai Yen and the cooperative members researched and perfected the processing formula, invested in a production line, designed packaging, and built the En Vang Crispy Rice brand. 
 To ensure its products are competitive in the market, the cooperative focuses on every stage, from selecting raw materials, quality control, processing, and packaging to ensuring food safety. This approach helps agricultural products go beyond simply consuming raw materials and elevate them into value-added goods. 
 In rural areas with many small-scale producers, increasing the value of agricultural products is one of the important ways to improve income. When products are processed, branded, and systematically distributed, the value created from agricultural production has a greater chance of being retained locally. 
 Livestream sessions selling agricultural products organized by Bui Thi Hai Yen. 
 Livestreaming sessions open up sales channels and create additional livelihoods. 
 To ensure product sales and enhance brand recognition, Hai Yen Cooperative proactively integrated digital transformation into its business operations. The cooperative's products are showcased on e-commerce platforms such as Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop; and online sales channels are being developed on Facebook and TikTok. The application of QR codes for product traceability has also been implemented to increase transparency and provide customers with more information about the products. 
 In particular, live streaming sessions conducted directly in the production area have become a hallmark of the cooperative's operations. 
 Through live broadcasts, producers can introduce their products and share stories about the ingredients, processing methods, and origin of their products with customers in various locations. 
 According to Ms. Hai Yen, livestreaming on social media helps farmers introduce and promote their products flexibly in terms of time and location. Customers can not only see the products but also learn about the process, origin, and source, thus having more basis for making a choice. 
 You may also like To conduct live stream sales of agricultural products, Bui Thi Hai Yen's team has to go directly to the farmers' gardens. 
 Notably, the livestream sessions of Ban Viet Cooperative not only serve its own business activities. The cooperative also supports the promotion and sale of products for many households and OCOP (One Commune One Product) entities in the area. 
 For small-scale producers with quality products but lacking the resources to establish their own sales channels, the connection provided by cooperatives can become a bridge to bring their goods closer to consumers. Instead of having to search for markets themselves, producers have more opportunities to reach customers through the cooperative's distribution and communication system. 
 From a poverty reduction perspective, this is a noteworthy approach. One of the difficulties faced by rural people lies not only in their production capacity but also in their ability to sell their products, find stable markets, and increase the value of their goods. 
 However, Hai Yen admitted that livestreaming also faced many difficulties. In the early days, the livestreaming team had to go directly to the orchards to film, but the locals didn't understand, and some even refused to let them touch the fruit for fear of damaging it. Besides that, when orders came in, transportation was a major problem. Many orders were damaged, forcing the team to compensate for losses and incur significant financial losses... 
 Bui Thi Hai Yen smiles alongside agricultural products. 
 Thanks to live streaming, local agricultural products have spread throughout the country. For example, previously, when people thought of custard apples, they only thought of Lang Son , but now, custard apples from Vo Nhai have been promoted, and their proven quality has become deeply ingrained in customers' minds. Therefore, custard apple trees have now become the main crop for the people of Vo Nhai, contributing to poverty reduction and increased income. 
 When output improves, production has a better chance of remaining stable, and people have more motivation to invest in product quality. For example, with Na Vo Nhai, people have now applied techniques to increase productivity, turning Na from one crop per year to two, and people's income has increased as a result, Hai Yen shared. 
 Increase the value of agricultural products and create jobs in our hometown. 
 After more than 3 years of operation, Ban Viet Cooperative has gradually established its brand in the market. Currently, the cooperative has 3 products that have achieved OCOP 3-star certification: En Vang Crispy Rice with Shredded Pork, En Ngoc Crispy Rice with Brown Rice, and Moc Huong Vegetarian Crispy Rice. 
 Along with product development, the cooperative built a showroom and store for regional agricultural products with an area of ​​over 150m2. It generates revenue of approximately 3 billion VND, with a profit of nearly 900 million VND, and provides regular employment for 15 local workers. 
 Notably, creating jobs locally provides workers with more income opportunities and reduces the need to seek employment far from their hometowns. 
 Bui Thi Hai Yen introduces agricultural products. 
 However, for such models to truly become a driving force in poverty reduction, it is crucial to expand linkages with production households, especially those facing difficulties in terms of capital, technology, and markets. Supporting people in improving product quality, participating in supply chains, and accessing modern sales methods will contribute to increasing the effectiveness of collective economic models. 
 For Ms. Hai Yen, the value of agricultural products lies not only in revenue or the quantity sold. The important thing is how to make local products a part of consumer life, carrying the cultural story and identity of the land that produces them. 
 Based on market realities, Ban Viet Cooperative aims to expand its range of specialty gift products, connecting typical products from various regions. 
 "We want to connect culture with local specialty products, linking the cultures of Thai Nguyen and Bac Kan after the merger so that a single gift box of specialties bears the mark of both regions," Ms. Hai Yen shared. 
 This idea not only opens up new avenues for product development but also demonstrates a new approach to exploiting the value of agricultural products. Each product can become a story about the land, people, customs, and culture; thereby creating differentiation in the market and increasing sales potential. 
 You may also like In the coming period, Ban Viet Cooperative aims to develop according to the ESG model, improve product quality, perfect the production and distribution chain, and promote the application of science and technology in management and business. 
 Mr. Jason Bay, Country Director (Vietnam market) of Sea Limited, visited Ban Viet Cooperative. 
 Based on the story of Ban Viet Cooperative, experts believe that sustainable poverty reduction begins not only with immediate support, but also with creating conditions for people to have jobs, markets, the ability to develop production, and self-reliance in their livelihoods. 
 Therefore, livestreaming sessions are not simply about selling products in the digital environment, but also a way to pave the way for agricultural products, create opportunities for workers, and contribute to building a sustainable rural economy. 
 For her efforts in developing the collective economy, enhancing the value of agricultural products, and creating livelihoods to help people escape poverty, Ms. Bui Thi Hai Yen was awarded the 20th Luong Dinh Cua Prize in 2025 by the Central Committee of the Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union. 
 In addition, the cooperative has received numerous commendations and certificates of merit in the fields of collective economic development, new rural construction, and OCOP product development. 
 The Ban Viet Cooperative has been assigned by the Thai Nguyen Provincial People's Committee and the Thai Nguyen Department of Industry and Trade to operate the province's shared store on the Shopee Vietnam e-commerce platform, making it the first shared agricultural product store in Vietnam. To date, the cooperative has organized over 125 live sessions on Shopee. 
 In particular, Mr. Jason Bay - Country Director (Vietnam market) of Sea Limited Group - visited Ban Viet Cooperative. 
 In early 2026, Ban Viet Cooperative will launch Ban Viet Restaurant and complete a one-cycle ecosystem of specialty agricultural products - from village to table. 
 Recently, Ban Viet officially established a chain of stores selling local agricultural products and regional specialties.
